review_metadata.scope: Primary benchmark targets and interpretation; no experiments reproduced
review_metadata.interpretation: Declared evaluation targets are not a population identification theorem. Access-limited papers are labeled separately.

records.title: Benchmarking atlas-level data integration in single-cell genomics
records.training_information: Multiple batches of common-feature RNA or ATAC data; some methods use labels; includes simulations.
records.target: Batch removal, cell-identity and label-free biological conservation, usability and scalability.
records.theorem_applicability: Horizontal-integration evaluation is not a test of completing a missing cross-assay joint or identifying direct cross-assay causal edges.
records.positive_restrictions: Empirical evidence of useful biological conservation remains valid for the tested tasks.
records.evidence_locator: Methods: Metrics; Ranking and metric aggregation; Results: scIB.
records.caveat: Published online December 2021, volume 19 in 2022. No new integration runs performed in this review.

records.title: Benchmarking multi-omics integration algorithms across single-cell RNA and ATAC data
records.training_information: Twelve integration methods across unpaired, paired and paired-guided tasks; paired datasets enable alignment evaluation.
records.target: Modality mixing, cell-type conservation, single-cell alignment, trajectory conservation, runtime and usability.
records.theorem_applicability: The reported metrics do not constitute a theorem or direct causal-DAG recovery benchmark.
records.positive_restrictions: Useful alignment and trajectory results must be preserved rather than relabeled causal failures.
records.evidence_locator: Introduction method categories; Discussion; Methods: trajectory conservation.
records.caveat: Anonymized paired reference views and truly independent disjoint samples are different statistical designs.

records.title: Benchmarking algorithms for single-cell multi-omics prediction and integration
records.training_information: Fourteen prediction algorithms and eighteen integration algorithms evaluated on 47 multimodal datasets.
records.target: Protein/chromatin prediction and multimodal integration accuracy, across several observation patterns.
records.theorem_applicability: Retained as evidence about declared benchmark scope only; no claim about all full-text theorem content is made.
records.positive_restrictions: Prediction and integration success are legitimate endpoints distinct from direct causal recovery.
records.evidence_locator: PubMed abstract PMID39322753; indexed publisher Extended Data Figs. 7–9.
records.caveat: Direct publisher HTML/PDF access returned an authentication redirect; PubMed page sometimes returned a browser check. Primary abstract and indexed publisher excerpts were available.

records.title: Benchmarking single-cell multi-modal data integrations
records.training_information: Forty algorithms across paired, unpaired and mosaic designs involving DNA, RNA, protein and spatial omics.
records.target: Usability, integration accuracy and robustness under dataset/quality variation.
records.theorem_applicability: Used to map method coverage and declared endpoints; no full-text absence-of-theorem conclusion drawn.
records.positive_restrictions: Different observation patterns must be compared separately.
records.evidence_locator: PubMed abstract and bibliographic record PMID40640531; indexed preprint metrics passage.
records.caveat: Publisher direct access failed; bioRxiv full-text request returned403. The primary abstract was read successfully.
records.conflicts: PubMed records authors declaring no competing interests.
records.funding: PubMed lists China Postdoctoral Science Foundation and National Natural Science Foundation of China grants.

records.method: Liu et al. multitask Registered Report
records.title: Multitask benchmarking of single-cell multimodal omics integration methods
records.training_information: Forty methods, four integration categories, real and simulated datasets; task-specific pairing/labels differ.
records.target: Dimension reduction, batch correction, clustering, classification, feature selection, imputation and spatial registration.
records.theorem_applicability: These seven tasks do not directly establish original-feature interventional graph identification.
records.positive_restrictions: The report notes that clustering/classification performance need not preserve structure relevant to imputation.
records.evidence_locator: Main: four categories/seven tasks; Discussion; Methods: evaluation pipelines; preregistered protocol link.
records.caveat: The 2024 bioRxiv protocol/version and the 2025 final publication are not two independent benchmark studies.

records.title: SCMBench: benchmarking domain-specific and foundation models for single-cell multi-omics data integration
records.training_information: Domain-specific and pretrained foundation models; paired/unpaired and batch-effect scenarios; simulations.
records.target: Cell-type integration accuracy, biological conservation, batch correction and marker/DAR/motif consistency.
records.theorem_applicability: Biological conservation and marker consistency do not establish original cross-assay causal edges. Pretrained references belong in the input-information contract.
records.positive_restrictions: Useful marker and alignment performance is not denied by a general nonidentifiability theorem.
records.evidence_locator: Methods: Evaluation metrics; Simulated data generation; Results: marker/DAR/motif evaluation.
records.caveat: Simulation uses a regulatory-network-based generator, but the inspected benchmark endpoints assess clustering/batch correction rather than exact recovery of that regulatory graph.

records.title: Benchmarking component choices for unpaired single cell RNA and epigenomic integration
records.training_information: Paired RNA/ATAC and RNA/histone data treated as unpaired for evaluation of feature linking, embeddings and labeling.
records.target: Gene-activity agreement, neighborhoods, same-cell matching proximity, clustering and label transfer; motivating peak–gene correlation case study.
records.theorem_applicability: Mislabeling can distort downstream pseudobulk correlations, but observed distortion is not a population impossibility proof or intervention ground truth.
records.positive_restrictions: Good neighborhood/clustering preservation can coexist with weak per-gene expression agreement; each target should be evaluated separately.
records.evidence_locator: Results: motivating example; Benchmarking GAS; dimension reduction; Methods; Figure1f–g.
records.caveat: Contains RNA with H3K4me1, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac references; no matrices were downloaded. Same-cell shuffling is not strict independent-disjoint sampling.
